findings.review_scope: Registered-source content review of Distributed Estimation and Inference for Semi-parametric Binary Response Models by Xi Chen, Wenbo Jing, Weidong Liu and Yichen Zhang. The registered file is arXiv:2210.08393v4, stamped 15 August 2024, with 102 physical pages. Main text and references occupy pages 1-40. Only the Appendix A heading at the top of page 41 was inspected; no appendix body was read. Fresh text evidence covers all forty in-scope pages. Rendered theorem, definition, assumption, context and boundary pages were inspected against the saved transcriptions.
findings.inventory: Eight actual Theorem headings occur: 3.1 on page 16, 3.3 on 19, 3.4 on 20, 4.1 and 4.2 on 24, 4.3 on 25, 5.1 on 28 and 5.2 on 29. Theorem 4.3 continues on page 27 after Algorithm 2 occupies page 26; Theorems 5.1 and 5.2 continue on pages 29 and 30. Proposition 3.2, Corollary 3.5, ordinary-font references and appendix results are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 3.1 retains Assumptions 1-5, the little-o machine bound, the n-based bandwidth, the nonzero direction, the centered normal limit and complete definition of U with its factorial sum and kernel constant. The population U is not confused with the empirical score.

Theorem 3.3 retains the dimension/initial-rate hypotheses, both bandwidth alternatives, all three rate terms and the exponent 2^(t-1) in the third term. Equation (13) is subsequent prose; its logarithmic iteration threshold is archived separately.

Theorem 3.4 retains its inherited assumptions, m and p growth restrictions, reference to (13), extra final iteration and bandwidth, directional quantifier, lambda_h bias power and negative lambda_h exponent in the variance denominator.

Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 retain Assumptions 1 and 5-9 and use distinct weighted estimators. Theorem 4.1 preserves the printed gtrsim minimum-batch condition and every weight, n/m_l factor and transpose in the sandwich variance. Theorem 4.2 preserves its generic initial error scale, unsuffixed m condition, two-stage bandwidth, barred U_W and V_W, inverse transpose and sufficiently-large-T qualifier.

Theorem 4.3 retains the inherited assumptions, epsilon bound, h_0 without an omega factor, later bandwidths, all four error terms and the explicit delta_m,0 definition with omega in its denominator. The algorithm page is not inserted into the original theorem statement.

Theorem 5.1 preserves the bounded-covariate and directional-second-moment conditions, dimension/local-size/sparsity growth, both initial error norms, delta_m,0=o(1), log m in the small-o hypothesis, log p in tuning and error bounds, every square-root placement and both forms of the l2 rate. The final l1 inequality is on an event of probability tending to one.

Theorem 5.2 preserves the full abbreviated statement, inherited assumptions, proper-bandwidth/parameter/kernel wording, iteration range, both rates and the infinitesimal r_m qualification. It does not add the separate post-theorem discussion or appendix-only tuning.
source_passages: All 25 source entries and twelve auxiliary excerpts were compared with the main text. Model (1), the iid baseline and normalization retain a coefficient of +1 for X, a signed binary response and possible dependence of noise on Z. Standing identification conditions (a)-(d) remain conditions on the law. Norms, stochastic order and asymptotic comparisons are supporting notation, not invented ranked definitions.

Assumptions 1-5 preserve the integrated higher-order kernel, moment cancellation and boundary conditions, distinct conditional density/CDF assumptions, conditional independence, both population matrices and the exponential-square covariate condition. Their original boundedness and strict eigenvalue wording are retained. No kernel positivity or empirical Hessian invertibility is added.

The SMSE, equal-batch average, local derivative sums and Algorithm 1 update match pages 12-14. The optional initialization construction is separate from the theorem rate assumption. The local minimizer is not a population minimizer, and the dense Newton update uses both global derivative averages.

Sections 4/4.1, Assumptions 6-9 and equations (16)-(18) preserve unequal machine sizes, a common coefficient, machine-specific density/noise CDFs, uniform derivative bounds and general matrix weights. A higher-resolution crop verifies the line-wrapped c_1 upper bound in Assumption 8. General weights are not silently restricted to positive scalar or positive-definite matrices. The source matrix-valued objective prose is kept separately from the operative weighted vector update.

Section 4.2 and Algorithm 2 preserve the first-machine target, target-equal set, equal local sizes and lack of covariate shift. They retain the floor(omega*m) selection sample, its threshold, complementary-observation derivatives normalized by (1-omega)*m, selected-machine averages and final output. No minimum coefficient separation condition is added.

Section 5 and equation (26) preserve the sparse coefficient and Dantzig-style constrained l1 update. The update uses a global gradient and the Hessian on machine 1; Algorithm 3 step 6 supplies the aggregation context. It does not require a global inverse-Hessian Newton step. The local bias constants, inherited hypothesis excerpts and explicit appendix deferral remain auxiliary passages.
findings.dependency_review: All 66 direct uses, 25 reach sets and 89 related connections were checked against their source meanings. Identifiability and kernel assumptions reach all eight theorems. Baseline iid sampling reaches 3.1/3.3/3.4/5.1/5.2, while the common law is overridden in the heterogeneous settings. Homogeneous density/CDF/population matrices additionally reach 4.3 through its inherited assumptions, with their local-model interpretation explicitly qualified. Machine-indexed regularity, weights and objectives reach only 4.1/4.2. SMSE minimization reaches 3.1/4.1/4.3; it is not required by the weighted Newton theorem. Dense Algorithm 1 reaches only 3.3/3.4. Algorithm 2 and coefficient shift reach only 4.3. Sparse parameter and constrained update reach only 5.1/5.2. Proof-only results, optional fitting methods, confidence-interval corollaries and appendix mathematics do not become dependencies.
findings.names_and_highlights: Each entry retains natural-language source keywords with its original heading and source kind. Numbered Assumptions 1-9 remain assumptions; unlabelled models, sampling conditions, identifiability and computational definitions remain distinguishable. All selectors were checked for their actual correspondence and occurrence in the source passage/label or a related same-paper theorem. Identical generic density/CDF terminology does not merge homogeneous and machine-specific assumptions. All related-theorem explanations retain a source-backed path.
findings.unresolved_scope: Theorem 5.2 retains one explicit outside_main_text_scope reference to Appendix A: proper choices of h_t, lambda_n^(t), H, and the formal definition of r_m. Main text calls r_m infinitesimal but does not supply those details. The completed main-text census does not claim to resolve them.
findings.source_limitations: All 27 existing source conventions were reviewed. These preserve preprint identity, normalization/coding differences, standing identification and heterogeneous sampling qualifications, signed kernels, differing uniformity wording, strict eigenvalue bounds, empirical versus population quantities, argmin/inverse conventions, initialization wording, rate exponents, bandwidth factors, c_w/c_W casing, general-weight invertibility issues, matrix-valued objective prose, gtrsim versus later little-o discussion, the unsuffixed m and unspecified large T, coefficient-shift inheritance, floor versus complementary normalization, omega factors, selection constants, local versus global Hessian, log m versus log p, sparse norm qualifications, appendix-only tuning and sequence-level uniformity. Source review establishes transcription and dependency fidelity; it does not certify proofs.
findings.changes: No census-content correction was required. All six saved census JSON artifacts and the original audit remain unchanged. Earlier Python scripts are archived. The paper rebuild now resolves the verified fixed local PDF and regenerates all six artifacts in an empty output directory; auxiliary inherited clauses use the saved original theorem transcription rather than loading an existing output inventory.
findings.validation: Both independent validators pass, and all six regenerated census artifacts match the saved bytes. Fresh source text, font-aware heading enumeration, source identity and boundary, interrupted theorem evidence, every direct/local edge set and reach set, paths, selector occurrences, artifact hashes and retention of unresolved appendix details supplement the manual source review.
